rationale: In the index delineation of KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder by Sleyp et al. (2022), the craniofacial features across the 14 evaluated individuals were characterized as 'subtle dysmorphic facial features' rather than presenting a recognizable, recurrent facial gestalt. Available literature confirms that the disorder is predominantly recognized by neurodevelopmental phenotypes (intellectual disability, febrile seizures/epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity) rather than a clear or distinctive craniofacial phenotype.

evidence.text: Sleyp et al. evaluated 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20 and identified a genetic syndrome characterized by mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features without a distinct recognizable facial gestalt.

evidence.text: OMIM entry 617679 records the phenotype as neurodevelopmental disorder with early-onset seizures, facial dysmorphism, and behavioral abnormalities (NEDSFBA) referencing Sleyp et al. (2022).

new_directions.question_text: Does computer-aided 3D facial photogrammetry or automated DeepGestalt analysis detect a sub-visual shared facial signature among KLHL20 missense variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: While clinical visual inspection classifies the facial dysmorphisms as subtle and variable, automated phenotyping pipelines may detect subtle geometric craniofacial patterns differentiating KLHL20 carriers from other neurodevelopmental cohorts.
